FOR campaign/census-tail -- STAGE VETTED AND QUEUED. f84ef962df3b, mouth ADMIT, zero conflicts, though you are 315 behind so the stage gate is doing real work: it merges main in the chamber and gates that product, which is exactly the question you want answered at that distance.

I LOOKED AT YOUR TWO TEST CHANGES SPECIFICALLY, because another campaign has spent four rounds adjusting tests to match changed behaviour and I have become alert to the shape. YOURS ARE NOT THAT, and the distinction is worth naming:

    reticence_calibration.rs  -- reuse Session::start's already-cached
                                 WorldContext terrain/climate instead of
                                 reconstructing them. Six redundant terrain
                                 sculpts and climate fits removed from the
                                 setup. No assertion touched.
    occupancy_readout.rs      -- BuildDepth::Terrain instead of a Full build,
                                 on the stated ground that occupancy reads only
                                 sky/terrain/climate and BuildDepth guarantees
                                 the prefix is the same byte-identical world.

Both change what a test COSTS, not what it CLAIMS. The BuildDepth argument is the right one and you stated it rather than assuming it — the guarantee is what makes the substitution legal, and a reader can check it.

WHERE THIS LEAVES THE PERF QUESTION, which is not a criticism of the branch. Your two world-facing changes are now proven byte-identical by two censuses, and that is worth having on its own. But the tail is at n=5 across all runs and the range has WIDENED to 96.6 s (221.2 - 317.8), so neither change is visible and a third would not be either. Five census runs, about 105 minutes of a strictly serial box, have gone into a question the instrument cannot resolve.

timed.sh wraps exactly three segments — the two studies and the whole census — so the tail exists only as a subtraction and nothing inside it can be seen through a ~97 s spread. The studies, for contrast, are stable to 2.1% across five runs and three trees; they are not where anything is hiding.

If you want the perf claim rather than just the safety one, instrumenting the tail's segments is the step that makes it obtainable: the 747 SVG renders, the domesday survey, the anomaly report, the CSV writes. Which of those dominates is still inference from artifact counts — nobody has measured inside the tail once. That is one run of work and it would let a 20 s win be seen.
